Triage: leveled finding → `pm:queue` / `domain:ui` / Task. Rationale: a dead pre-ADR-0079 resolver copy, exported from a utils module console code already imports — dead code plus a re-armed trap for exactly the failure ADR-0079 closed (a same-named, same-signature resolver one import away that ignores every declared pointer). Deleting both `getRecordDisplayName` and `formatRecordTitle` from `apps/console/src/utils.ts` restores the single-resolver invariant; prefer deletion over a re-export alias per the card's own reasoning. Dispatch note: re-run the liveness grep at fix time — several seats edit the console. Size: S, mechanical.

## 1. The ruling

Triage: delete **both** `getRecordDisplayName` and `formatRecordTitle` from `apps/console/src/utils.ts`. ⛔ Prefer deletion over a re-export alias, per the card's own reasoning — a re-export would keep the trap armed under a different spelling.

## 2. Liveness census — triage asked for this at fix time; here is mine, re-run it

**Every mention of either name in the whole of `apps/console` is inside `utils.ts` itself.** Three lines:

```
:45   export function formatRecordTitle(titleFormat, record)
:73   export function getRecordDisplayName(objectDef, record)
:75     return formatRecordTitle(objectDef.titleFormat, record);
```

Zero importers. The only import from the console's own `utils` module anywhere is `resolveKeyedI18nLabel` at `AppManagementPage.tsx:70`, a different symbol.

⭐ `:75` is the detail that makes the pair-deletion correct rather than merely convenient: **`formatRecordTitle`'s only caller is `getRecordDisplayName`**, the other dead function. They are a closed pair — deleting one without the other leaves a function with zero callers. And `:73-:75` confirms the card's claim about the inverted ranking: it returns the `titleFormat` template **before** consulting anything else, which is exactly the ordering ADR-0079 Phase 2 inverted.

## 3. ⛔⛔ The name has THREE homes. Two of them are correct and must survive.

This is the part the card does not say, and the part most likely to turn an S card into a regression. `formatRecordTitle` is **not** console-local:

| # | location | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `apps/console/src/utils.ts:45` | **the dead copy — yours to delete** |
| 2 | `packages/app-shell/src/utils/index.ts:15` — `formatTitleTemplate as formatRecordTitle` | ⛔ **deliberate back-compat alias.** Documented at `:7`, `:14` and `:107` with an explicit ADR-0079 note. Do not touch. |
| 3 | `packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx:80` | ⛔ **private local function with REVERSED arguments** — `(record, titleFormat)`, not `(titleFormat, record)`. Do not touch, and do not "converge" it: the signatures are not compatible. |

A search for the name hits all three. Only the first is dead.

⚠️ **There is a gate that tracks this name**: `scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts:481` records the app-shell alias as a known entry. Deleting the console copy changes the population that gate sees. Run it and report what it says — if it needs an inventory update, that is a real part of this card; if it goes green untouched, say so. ⛔ Do **not** edit that inventory to make a red go away without telling me — that is gate weakening, and the failure text is a generic remedy, not this file's ruling.

## 4. One path ambiguity that will bite

`apps/console/src/` contains **both** a file `utils.ts` and a directory `utils/` (e.g. `utils/getIcon.ts`, referenced by `scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs:168`). Your target is the **file**. Confirm which one you have open before editing.

## 5. Scope

`apps/console/src/utils.ts` only, plus a changeset if the gates say one is owed — `apps/console` may not be a released package, so **ask `check-changeset-presence` for its verdict rather than assuming** either way.

Shadow check: no in-flight card touches `apps/console/src/utils.ts`. ⚠️ **#3719 is in flight in `apps/console/src/pages/settings/`** — a different directory, but the same app. If you find yourself editing anything under `pages/settings/`, stop and tell me.

## 6. Verification

Deletion cards are easy to prove wrongly. Show that the build and typecheck still pass **and** that they would have caught a live importer — i.e. establish the check is capable of failing, not merely that it passed. Re-run the liveness grep immediately before pushing: triage's note says several seats edit the console, and my census above is minutes old, not current.

⭐ Verify my three-homes table independently. Your reading wins, and this seat has produced false zeros from guessed paths and over-narrow patterns repeatedly today.

**Post-merge verification — PR #6571 merged 2026-08-26T14:04:48Z. Measured on `main`, all axes clean.**

Read back from `main` through the contents API, not from the PR diff, because a diff shows what was proposed and `main` shows what landed.

**The fix.** `apps/console/src/utils.ts` is 44 lines and declares neither function — zero matches for a `function`/`const` declaration of `formatRecordTitle` or `getRecordDisplayName`. The only surviving mentions are the two explanatory lines of the removal comment (`:37`, `:43`), which point a future reader at the unified `@object-ui/core#getRecordDisplayName` rather than leaving the deletion unexplained.

**Control — the file's live export was not collateral damage.** `resolveKeyedI18nLabel` is still exported at `:15`. That matters here more than usual: it is the *only* thing anything in the console imports from this file, so a deletion that took it would have been a real breakage hiding behind a green "dead code removed" claim.

**The two deliberate NON-removals both survived.** This is the half worth checking, because a same-named symbol in three places is exactly the shape a cleanup over-reaches on:

| site | expected | measured on `main` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `packages/app-shell/src/utils/index.ts:15` | back-compat alias kept | present — `formatTitleTemplate as formatRecordTitle`, with its ADR-0079 notes intact at `:7`, `:14`, `:107` |
| `packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx:80` | private local kept, reversed signature | present — `function formatRecordTitle(record: any, titleFormat: string)`, still called at `:127` |

So the deletion hit exactly the one dead copy it was scoped to and neither look-alike was swept in with it. Nothing outstanding on this card.
